an Australian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Guerri Napoli]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played four seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]] before debuting in the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) in 2020 for [[Melbourne United]]. After two seasons in the NBL, he debuted in the [[NBA]] in 2022 for the [[Denver Nuggets]] and won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] while part of the Nuggets roster in 2023. ==Early life and career== White was born in [[Traralgon]], [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]].{{cite web|title=Jack White - January 2016 |language=en}} He made his NBL debut on 15 January against [[Melbourne United]], playing four minutes. ==College career== In 2016, White moved to the United States to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]].{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Tyler|title=Aussie Jack White living his dream with Duke Blue Devils and Coach K|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22115886/aussie-jack-white-living-dream-duke-blue-devils-coach-k|work=[[ESPN]]|date=18 January 2018|access-date=18 January 2018}} As a freshman in [[2016–17 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2016–17]], White played in 10 games and averaged 2.1 points and 1.3 rebounds in 6.1 minutes per game. As a sophomore in [[2017–18 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2017–18]], he played in 28 games and averaged 1.5 rebounds in 5.7 minutes per game. Prior to his junior year, White was named [[captain (sports)|team captain]]. In [[2018–19 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2018–19]], he appeared in a career-best 35 games and made three starts. He totaled career highs in minutes (20.4), rebounds (4.7), and points (4.1) per game. He registered career highs in 3-pointers made (4-for-6) and points (12) against [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] on 5 January 2019. He earned [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Academic selection. As a senior in [[2019–20 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2019–20]], White played in 30 games with seven starts, averaging 3.1 points and 2.9 rebounds in 15.6 minutes per game. He again served as team captain and was again named to the ACC All-Academic team.{{cite news|first=Rick|last=Bouch|title=Season Recap: Jack White|url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Article/Season-Recap-Jack-White-146055148/|work=247 Sports|date=14 April 2020|access-date=15 April 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Melbourne United (2020–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], White signed a three-year deal with [[Melbourne United]] of the NBL on 15 July 2020.{{cite web|title=Duke Standout Jack White Signs with Melbourne {{!}} NBL|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/duke-standout-jack-white-signs-with-melbourne|website=NBL.com.au|access-date=15 July 2020|archive-date=24 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230324142700/https://nbl.com.au/news/duke-standout-jack-white-signs-with-melbourne|url-status=dead}} In April 2021, he suffered a season-ending Achilles injury.{{cite news |title=Jack White's Incredible Journey |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/jack-white-s-incredible-journey |access-date=22 December 2024 |work=NBL Official Website |date=21 July 2022}} United went on to win the [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]] in the [[2020–21 NBL season|2020–21 season]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/united-secure-nbl21-championship-on-home-court|title=United secure NBL21 championship on home court|website=NBL.com.au|date=25 June 2021|access-date=25 June 2021}} White returned to action for United in December 2021. Following the [[2021–22 NBL season]], White had a four-game stint with the [[Geelong Supercats]] of the [[NBL1 South]], averaging 20 points and 12.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Oorschot |first1=Vinnie van |title=Former Supercat relishes milestone of a lifetime |url=https://timesnewsgroup.com.au/geelongtimes/sport/former-supercat-relishes-milestone-of-a-lifetime/ |access-date=22 December 2024 |work=Geelong Times |date=24 June 2023 |language=en-AU}}{{cite news |title=Geelong Supercat Jack White headed to the Denver Nuggets |url=https://nbl1.com.au/article/geelong-supercat-jack-white-headed-to-the-denver-nuggets |access-date=22 December 2024 |work=nbl1.com.au |date=18 July 2022}} ===Denver Nuggets (2022–2023)=== In July 2022, White played for the [[Denver Nuggets]] in [[2022 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]] and signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Nuggets for the [[2022–23 Denver Nuggets season|2022–23 season]].{{cite web|title=Nuggets Sign Jack White to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-jack-white-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=19 July 2022|access-date=20 July 2022}} He played the majority of the season with the [[Grand Rapids Gold]] in the [[NBA G League]], averaging 20.9 points, 9.6 boards, 0.9 steals and 0.8 blocks per game in 14 games.{{cite news |title=Aussie Jack White No. 1 pick in G League draft |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/38769013/aussie-jack-white-no-1-pick-g-league-draft-keeps-nba-dream-alive |access-date=22 December Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whiteja03.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=22 December 2024 |language=en}} He scored an NBA season high of seven points on 25 February 2023 against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web |title=Jack White 2022-23 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whiteja03/gamelog/2023/ Denver Nuggets |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/aussie-jack-white-wins-nba-championship-with-denver-nuggets/news-story/90cda74cb8d74d8eb3b90a71abf3399f |access-date=22 December 2024 ==National team career== White debuted for Australia at the 2013 [[FIBA U15 Oceania Cup|FIBA Oceania U16 Championship]].{{cite web |title=Jack White |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/205900-jack-white |website=FIBA |access-date=22 December 2024}} He played at the 2014 [[FIBA U17 Oceania Cup|FIBA Oceania U18 Championship]] and then won a silver medal at the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] in [[Dubai]]. At the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] in [[Heraklion]], White averaged 8.3 points and 3.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Australia's Jack White looks to take next step|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/news/australias-jack-white-looks-to-take-next-step|website=FIBA.basketball|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=15 March 2016|access-date=15 April 2020}} In 2019, White helped the Australia national university team win bronze at the [[Basketball at the 2019 Summer Universiade|Summer Universiade]] in Italy.{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Connelly|title=Jack White wins Bronze Medal for Australia at World University Games|url=https://balldurham.com/2019/07/11/jack-white-wins-bronze-medal-australia-world-university-games/|website=BallDurham.com|publisher=Ball Durham|date=11 July 2019|access-date=15 April 2020}} White made his [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]] debut during the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|2023 FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers]]. In July 2022, he had 16 points and 14 rebounds in a game against [[China men's national basketball team|China]].{{cite news |title=White leads Boomers to big win over China |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/34188060/jack-white-leads-boomers-big-win-china |access-date=22 December 2024 |work=ESPN.com |date=3 July 2022 |language=en}} He played for the Boomers at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. In July 2025, White was named in the Boomers squad in the lead up to the [[2025 FIBA Asia Cup]] in Saudi Arabia.{{cite news |title=Balanced Boomers for University of Colorado |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4300205/balanced-boomers-for-university-of-colorado |access-date=3 July 2025 |work=www.australia.basketball |date=3 July 2025 |language=en}}{{cite news |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=Generationally diverse extended Australian Boomers squad named |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/45650023/generationally-diverse-extended-australian-boomers-squad-named |access-date=3 July 2025 |work=ESPN.com |date=3 July 2025 |language=en}} In October 2025, White was named in the Boomers squad for the first window of the [[2027 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers]].{{cite news |title=Boomers confirmed for NZ double-header |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4388280/boomers-confirmed-for-nz-double-header |access-date=24 October 2025 |work=www.australia.basketball |date=24 October 2025 |language=en}} In February 2026, he was named in the squad for two more Asian qualifiers.{{cite news |title=Boomers eye next phase of World Cup qualification |url=https://www.australia.basketball/news/4441021/boomers-eye-next-phase-of-world-cup-qualification |access-date=18 February 2026 |work=www.australia.basketball |date=18 February 2026 |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=y}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;
